short_definition: Touch arising while a person deliberately explores an object.
full_definition: Touch perception produced through self-directed movement, where motor commands and sensory feedback jointly support perception.

short_definition: Control that maps measured force to commanded motion.
full_definition: A haptic control architecture in which force or torque is the input and desired position or velocity is the output.

short_definition: Sensory nerve fibre carrying information toward the central nervous system.
full_definition: A neural pathway that transmits information from receptors in skin, muscles, tendons, or joints toward the spinal cord and brain.

short_definition: Misrepresentation caused by inadequate sampling.
full_definition: The appearance of false lower-frequency components when a signal is sampled below the rate required to represent its highest relevant frequencies.

short_definition: Perceived motion created by sequential stationary stimuli.
full_definition: A percept of movement across the skin produced by activating spatially separated tactors with suitable timing.

short_definition: Frequency range over which a system performs adequately.
full_definition: The span of frequencies a sensor, actuator, controller, or communication channel can reproduce or measure within specified limits.

short_definition: Alignment of information across coordinate systems or modalities.
full_definition: The spatial and temporal alignment between visual, haptic, tracked, and physical elements so that they refer to the same apparent location and event.

short_definition: Deformation per unit force.
full_definition: The inverse of stiffness in a linear model; a compliant object deforms substantially under applied load.

short_definition: Perception mediated primarily by receptors in the skin.
full_definition: Tactile information arising from skin deformation, vibration, pressure, stretch, temperature, and related cues.

short_definition: Velocity-dependent resistance.
full_definition: A mechanical property that dissipates energy and produces a force often modelled as proportional to relative velocity.

short_definition: Smallest stimulus reliably distinguishable from no stimulus.
full_definition: A psychophysical estimate of the stimulus magnitude associated with a chosen probability of detection.

short_definition: Experience of a body or representation as one’s own and under one’s control.
full_definition: A family of perceptual phenomena involving body ownership, agency, and self-location in physical or virtual environments.

short_definition: Friction modulation using an electrostatic force.
full_definition: A surface-haptics technique that changes the apparent friction between a finger and an insulated electrode by applying a time-varying voltage.

short_definition: Haptic output that applies mechanical force or torque to the user.
full_definition: A class of kinesthetic interface that resists or guides movement to represent contact, weight, constraints, or dynamics.

short_definition: Output magnitude and phase as a function of input frequency.
full_definition: A system characterization showing how sensors, actuators, or complete haptic devices transform sinusoidal inputs across frequency.

short_definition: Computation of haptic output from an interactive model.
full_definition: The real-time process that estimates contact and object behaviour, then generates commands for a haptic device.

short_definition: Science and engineering of touch-mediated perception and interaction.
full_definition: The interdisciplinary study and design of systems through which people perceive, communicate, or act using tactile, kinesthetic, proprioceptive, thermal, and related bodily information.

short_definition: Relationship between motion and force.
full_definition: Mechanical impedance describes how a system resists motion; in control, impedance methods map displacement or velocity error to force.

short_definition: Control that maps motion error to force.
full_definition: A haptic control architecture that specifies a target dynamic relationship between position or velocity and interaction force.

short_definition: Smallest reliably discriminable change in a stimulus.
full_definition: A difference threshold, usually defined at a selected correct-response level on a psychometric function.

short_definition: Perception of force, position, and movement of limbs.
full_definition: Information arising primarily from muscles, tendons, joints, and large-scale skin deformation that contributes to movement and force perception.

short_definition: Delay between an event and the corresponding system response.
full_definition: Elapsed time from sensing or user action to rendered output; delay can reduce realism and destabilize closed-loop haptic systems.

short_definition: Psychophysical method using numerical estimates of perceived strength.
full_definition: A scaling procedure in which participants assign numbers proportional to the apparent intensity or quality of stimuli.

short_definition: Sensory receptor responsive to mechanical deformation.
full_definition: A receptor that transduces indentation, stretch, vibration, force, or motion into neural activity.

short_definition: Combination of information from multiple sensory modalities.
full_definition: The process by which the nervous system combines visual, auditory, tactile, proprioceptive, and other signals, often weighting them by reliability and context.

short_definition: Touch produced without deliberate exploratory movement.
full_definition: Tactile stimulation delivered to a relatively stationary body location, typically with reduced contribution from self-generated motor commands.

short_definition: Property of a system that cannot generate net energy.
full_definition: An energy-based condition used in haptic control to reason about stability when a device interacts with a user and virtual environment.

short_definition: Percept located between or away from physical tactors.
full_definition: A spatial tactile percept created by simultaneous or patterned stimulation at multiple skin locations.

short_definition: Sense of body position and movement.
full_definition: Somatosensory information about limb configuration, muscle state, and movement, derived from muscle, tendon, joint, and cutaneous cues.

short_definition: Relationship between stimulus magnitude and response probability.
full_definition: A fitted curve used to estimate thresholds
related_terms: and discrimination performance from psychophysical data.

short_definition: Quantitative study of relations between physical stimuli and perception.
full_definition: Methods and models for measuring detection, discrimination, perceived magnitude, and decision behaviour.

short_definition: Region where stimulation changes a sensory neuron’s activity.
full_definition: The spatial area of skin, muscle, or another sensory surface associated with a particular afferent or neuron.

short_definition: Large response near a system’s natural frequency.
full_definition: A frequency-dependent amplification that occurs when periodic input couples strongly to a mechanical or electrical mode.

short_definition: Tactile illusion in which discrete stimuli appear to jump across the skin.
full_definition: A spatiotemporal illusion where a sequence delivered at a few physical locations is perceived at intermediate positions.

short_definition: Repeated sensing-computation-actuation cycle.
full_definition: A real-time control loop that updates haptic forces or tactile commands, often at a substantially higher rate than the graphics loop.

short_definition: Framework separating sensitivity from decision bias.
full_definition: A model that describes detection and discrimination using distributions of internal responses, producing measures such as d-prime and criterion.

short_definition: Ability to resolve nearby tactile locations or patterns.
full_definition: Perceptual spatial resolution, which depends on body site, receptor density, stimulus type, and task.

short_definition: Change in force per unit displacement.
full_definition: For a linear spring, stiffness k relates force and displacement by F = kx; perceived stiffness also depends on dynamics and exploration.

short_definition: Relating to sensations primarily arising at the skin.
full_definition: A term often used for cutaneous feedback such as vibration, pressure, skin stretch, friction modulation, or temperature.

short_definition: Remote control with sensory feedback.
full_definition: Interaction in which a human commands a distant robot or system and receives visual, auditory, haptic, or other feedback from the remote environment.

short_definition: Use of heating or cooling as interactive feedback.
full_definition: Haptic interfaces that control skin temperature or heat flow to convey material, event, affective, or environmental information.

short_definition: Task requiring selection between two alternatives.
full_definition: A psychophysical procedure in which the observer chooses which of two intervals or stimuli contains a target or has a greater attribute.

short_definition: Compliant connection between a device and virtual proxy.
full_definition: A spring-damper or related dynamic element inserted between the physical haptic interface and virtual object to improve stability and manage constraints.

short_definition: Ratio of JND to reference magnitude.
full_definition: A normalized discrimination measure, ΔI/I, that is approximately constant over some stimulus ranges but not universally.
